### Executive Summary
* A third pre-authentication Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability has been identified affecting SonicWall SMA 1000 series appliances.
* The flaw allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to leverage the appliance as a proxy to issue network requests on the attacker's behalf.

### Technical Impact & Root Cause
* The root cause stems from an unauthenticated SSRF entry point within the SonicWall SMA 1000 interface.
* Successful exploitation enables unauthenticated attackers to manipulate the appliance into making outbound or lateral HTTP/network requests, potentially exposing internal services or evading boundary security controls.

### Mitigation & IOCs
* Specific patch information and mitigation steps were not detailed in the source content. Administrators relying on SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances should monitor official SonicWall security advisories for firmware updates.
